segment.description: Big Rock Creek, Marshall County, Tennessee (catalog) — a small Duck River tributary through Lewisburg, rising in southwest Marshall County and flowing north about 20 river miles to its confluence with the Duck River (TDEC's nearest mainstem station is described as 'HIGHWAY 272 DOWNSTEAM BIG ROCK CREEK' at 35.577, -86.779, HUC 06040002). Catalog YAML carries no counties field; identity resolved from the catalog hydroIdentity (GNIS 01305230, HUC8 06040002) and confirmed against WQP station metadata: every 'Big Rock Creek' station found sits in HUC 06040002 with county code 117 (Marshall), matching the catalog note 'TWRA winter-stocked Marshall County creek near Lewisburg'. Same-named Big Rock Creeks elsewhere in Tennessee were not an issue here — all stations returned by the Marshall County sweep belong to this creek.
segment.boundaries: The named Big Rock Creek within Marshall County (HUC 06040002); identity stations USGS-03599000 'BIG ROCK CREEK AT LEWISBURG, TN' (24.9 sq mi, alt 705.01 ft NGVD29) and USGS-03599100 'BIG ROCK CR AT DOUBLE BRIDGES, TN' (48.7 sq mi, alt 644.37 ft). TWRA's stocking-site string is 'Big Rock Greenway' (Region 2, Marshall) with no reach detail; the greenway lies along the creek in Lewisburg, so in-town gauge USGS-03599000 is the nearest temperature station to the stocking site.

coldSource.notes: Elevation 705.01 ft is the USGS-03599000 station altitude at Lewisburg (NGVD29); the downstream Double Bridges station sits at 644.37 ft — a low-relief agricultural/urban Marshall County valley with no gorge or canopy documentation found. No cold-water source of any kind documented. TDEC station TDECWPC-BROCK006.0ML is described as '100 YARDS DOWNSTREAM DAM AT VERONA', evidencing an unnamed small dam on the creek at Verona; no operator or release documentation exists, and the 26.3 deg C July 2000 grab below it shows no cold-release effect. Identity verified from WQP station metadata columns (station names, Marshall County code 117, HUC 06040002) because the USGS identity endpoint has been 503ing this week.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. The TWRA program is winter-only catchable rainbows at 'Big Rock Greenway': 2026 workbook rows (Region 2, Marshall, type Winter, Rainbow Trout) are 1/15/2026, 2/27/2026 and TBD 12/2026; the live TWRA stocking page contains the 'Big Rock Greenway' site string (fetched copy's flattened table interleaves two tables, so its stray date cells cannot be attributed). No source documents survival between stockings or through summer, and the in-town summer record (USGS-03599000 nearest the greenway: 24.7-32.0 deg C June-September grabs) makes summer survival implausible on the cited temperatures alone.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found in any agency source for Big Rock Creek. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Tennessee's wild trout in East Tennessee and describes hatchery-supported streams and lakes as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' (canon quote; PDF not fetched per rule).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: 91 June-September grab samples across 1966-2025 on every reach of Big Rock Creek run 18.5-32.0 deg C — 25.3-32.0 deg C at the in-town Lewisburg gauge nearest the Big Rock Greenway stocking site — far above year-round trout survival thresholds.
